title: Fall of the bound pair one order beyond leading order

key_results.statement: Exactly, $1+r_i=-\varsigma\bar s(\mathfrak m_1+\mathfrak m_2)E_b''(0)\langle\sigma^{(i)}_3\rangle_0$ and $1+r_X=-\varsigma\bar s(\mathfrak m_1+\mathfrak m_2)E_b''(0)$, for every diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$ and all three gradients.

At fixed $u\in(0,\infty)$, $r_i=-\beta_i(1+\varsigma/\bar s)-\frac{\varsigma\bar s}{4a}\mathcal C+O(\epsilon^4)$ and $r_X=-\frac{\varsigma\bar s}{4a}\mathcal C+O(\epsilon^4)$, with $\mathcal C$ of (14.9), both signs $\varsigma$.

For the common gradient $g_{\rm c}\neq0$ and $\langle X\rangle=0$: $\mathcal W/g_{\rm c}-E_b(0)=-\varsigma a(\bar s+\varsigma)^2/\bar s+\mathcal V_4+O(\epsilon^6)$, with $\mathcal V_4=(u\partial_u-4)\mathcal E_4=\frac{\gamma_s}{2}\psi_A+\frac{\gamma_s+\gamma_m}{2}\psi_B$; at order $\epsilon^2$ the binding cost is weighed with the factor $-\varsigma/\bar s$, and the order-$\epsilon^2$ difference is nonzero for every $u\in(0,\infty)$ and both signs, with sign $-\varsigma$.
$\psi_A=8-2u^2+(8\varsigma+10\varsigma u^2+u^3+2u^5)/\bar s^3$ and $\psi_B=2u^2+(2\varsigma u^2-u^3+3\varsigma u^4-2u^5)/\bar s^3$.

For $g_{\rm c}\neq0$ and $\langle X\rangle=0$, exactly $a_{\rm pair}/\bar a-1=(\delta_W-\delta_{\mathfrak m})/(1+\delta_{\mathfrak m})$, with the relative changes $\delta_W$ of the weight against $g_{\rm c}(M_1+M_2)$ and $\delta_{\mathfrak m}$ of the inertia against $\mathfrak m_1+\mathfrak m_2$.
$\delta_W=-\frac{a}{M_1+M_2}(1+\varsigma/\bar s)+O(\epsilon^4)$ and $1+\delta_{\mathfrak m}=-\varsigma\bar s(1+\mu)+O(\epsilon^4)$, with $\mu=\frac{\varsigma\bar s}{4a}\mathcal C$.

Through relative order $\epsilon^2$ at fixed $u$: $a_{\rm pair}/\bar a-1=-1-\varsigma/\bar s+c_2+O(\epsilon^4)$, with $c_2=\frac{\varsigma}{\bar s}\frac{a}{M_1+M_2}(1+\frac{\varsigma}{\bar s})+\frac{\mathcal C}{4a}$.

For $w_{11}<0$ in the ordered limit: the order-$\epsilon^2$ coefficient of item 2 is $\frac a4u^4+O(u^6)$ and the order-$\epsilon^4$ coefficient is $-\frac12\gamma_mu^3+O(u^5)$, with $\gamma_m>0$ for all data, so its leading term vanishes on no data.

For $w_{11}<0$ in the ordered limit: $c_2=K_2u^2+O(u^3)$ with $K_2=\frac{a(M_1+M_2)}{2M_1M_2}[(x_1-y_2)^2-2x_1x_2]$, $x_i=a_i/a$, $y_i=M_i/(M_1+M_2)$; $K_2=0$ if and only if $x_1=\frac13(1+y_2\pm\sqrt{1+2y_1y_2})$, two surfaces that meet every ratio $M_1/M_2$ and exclude equal data.

definitions.name: relative correction of the pair inertia
order-epsilon^4 coefficient of weight minus cost
order-epsilon^2 correction of the pair-to-parts ratio
wide-pair coefficient of the ratio correction

open_issues: Joint limits in ε and u are out of scope: at ς=−1 the order-ε² coefficient of item 2 is O(u⁴) and the order-ε⁴ one is O(u³), so which dominates depends on how ε and u go to zero together.
On the two surfaces where K_2=0 the leading term of c_2 is not determined (restricted by the question).
Item 2 compares W/g_c with E_b(0) in the zero of the cost fixed by G_i=M_i σ_3; couplings to other operators (criterion 6) are not treated.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of r_i, r_X, δ_W, δ_m, c_2, K_2 (dimensionless) and of V_4 and W/g_c − E_b(0) (costs)
Ordered limit u→0 at ς=−1: all remainders and both coefficients of item 2 vanish, the wide pair falls with the mean of its parts and weighs its cost
Order-ε⁴ coefficient of item 2 at small u recomputed from the X_k of (14.12) and the expansion of (14.7): −γ_m u³/2 + 0·u⁴ − γ_m u⁵/4

response_to_verification.where: Setup and assumptions (notation and regime R, orders); Step 1(b)
